subject: Capacity chokepoint: PayCore reserved throughput shortfall and exec bridge
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@paycore.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hernandez <tom.hernandez@paycore.com>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden spike in errors — reserved capacity not honoring throughput

Rachel —

We started seeing a sustained increase in 429/503 errors around 09:30 PT today and the p95 latency for our highest-volume route jumped from ~220ms to >1.6s. This is happening for requests that should be on our reserved capacity (we're on Dedicated-XL). Our throughput dropped by roughly 25% during the window even though tokens used are within our commit. The errors are causing retries in our pipeline and customers are noticing.

I've attached the CSV with the error ramp and a screenshot of the latency distribution. Can you confirm whether this is on your side (pool saturation) or if we need to change anything on our end? This is impacting our billing cycle and an internal incident is already open. We need a clear timeline for remediation and any mitigation we can apply immediately.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform, PayCore
From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: sudden spike in errors — PayCore reserved capacity

Team — forwarding an urgent customer report from PayCore (DEAL-3482). Key points:
- PayCore observes sustained p95 latency >1.6s and ~25% throughput degradation despite being on Dedicated-XL reserved pool.
- Errors are 429/503; payloads small, traffic pattern steady (not massive CT spikes).
- Customer impact: retries and user-visible errors; ops incident open.

Can ops/infra triage and confirm whether there was pool saturation or a scheduling/regression in routing that caused reserved requests to spill? Marcus/Jordan, please prioritize an initial incident triage and costed remediation options (2hr, 6hr, 24hr).

Also copying Marissa/Monica for customer comms and to escalate to Sales/CS exec if needed. Sean — asking for exec attention in case we need priority headroom or credits.

Attachments: paycore_error_ramp_log_0503.csv, p95_latency_by_route_0503.png

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden spike in errors — PayCore reserved capacity

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Checked Dedicated-XL pool for us-west-2 host group between 09:00-10:30 PT. Observed elevated queue_depth on GPU nodes pinned to PayCore's reservation (queue spikes coincident with latency ramp).
- Autoscaler behavior: no global scale-up triggered because reserved nodes are at allocation limit; excess traffic spilled to shared pools causing intermittent throttling and engineered 503s from fallback logic.
- No obvious kernel or model regression flagged in runtime logs during window; kernel/pipeline latencies nominal per-node.

Immediate mitigations we can do (ordered by speed):
1) Short-term: temporarily bump PayCore to a higher burst quota (add 2-4 standby GPUs) and shift their routing to avoid shared pool spill for 2-6 hours. Needs exec approval for emergency headroom.
2) Mid-term (6-24h): adjust routing policy to enforce hard isolation for reserved commitments when SLOs are at risk, plus increase autoscaler sensitivity to queue depth for reserved pools.
3) Long-term: capacity planning follow-up, prefer oversubscription buffer for adjacent capacity tiers.

I'll open OPS ticket OPS-1234 with logs; Jordan, can you validate the spill fingerprints and check whether prefix cache sharding caused uneven node load?

—Marcus Lin
Head of Infra Operations
Redwood Inference
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden spike in errors — PayCore reserved capacity

I dug into the request distribution and KV cache hit rates. Findings:
- Hot-prefix concentration: ~35% of PayCore requests hit two KV shards which were co-located on a subset of dedicated nodes — explains localized queueing despite overall capacity headroom.
- There's a fallback path that shunts to shared inference lane when per-node queue depth exceeds threshold; that path returns 429/503 intermittently when downstream shared nodes are saturated.

Short-term actions I can implement within the hour:
- Redistribute KV shard placement for PayCore to spread hot prefixes (canary; low-risk).
- Tighten fallback backoff window so retries back off instead of immediate spikes.

I'll run the shard rebalancing at 16:45 PT and monitor metrics. If Marcus can provision the 2 standby GPUs as a safety valve, we should get customer impact down quickly.

—Jordan Blake
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
